chat_response.message: The governed workflow recommends **increase**. A modest increase appears supportable because claims performance weakened while trading indicators and market context remained broadly stable. The loss ratio moved from 71.8% to 82.4%, indicating materially weaker profitability, and the claims specialist also reported higher average severity and incurred loss with broadly stable frequency, so deterioration was associated more with claim cost than volume [claims-north_west-2025-12-01]. At the same time, quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 22.0% and renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 88.1%, which suggests no clear evidence of current trading stress in aggregate [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01]. External positioning is also consistent with a modest upward move: tracked competitors showed average price-index movement of +2.5%, and supporting market, broker, repair-cost, and feedback evidence described moderate market firming, stable competitive positioning, repair-cost inflation, limited broker pushback, and no concentrated pattern of price complaints [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-market-2025-11, doc-repair-cost-2025-10, doc-broker-2025-12, doc-broker-2025-09, doc-feedback-2025-11]. The proposed 2% to 4% range stays within the stated policy limit and is directionally consistent with the prior recorded +2.0% pricing action [pricing-history-2024-06-01]. This is decision support only and needs an analyst’s explicit confirmation before any action is recorded.

specialist_reports.summary: For the period 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-01, claim frequency was broadly stable, moving from 0.0844 to 0.0840, a change of -0.55%. Average severity increased from £1,615.2992 to £1,863.9629, up 15.39%. Incurred loss increased from £682,120.0492 to £781,847.0825, up 14.62%. Loss ratio increased from 0.7183 to 0.8244, up 14.77%. Overall, weaker claims performance was associated with materially higher average severity, higher incurred loss, and a higher loss ratio, while claim frequency remained essentially flat.

For the period 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-01, quote-to-sale conversion was 21.85% at baseline and 21.95% currently, a 0.46% increase. Renewal retention was 87.97% at baseline and 88.06% currently, a 0.11% increase. Average quoted premium was £621.5842 at baseline and £620.9067 currently, a 0.11% decrease.

The small improvement in quote-to-sale conversion coincided with a slight reduction in average quoted premium. Retention was broadly stable, with only a marginal uplift over the period.

By segment, new business conversion was 14.99% at baseline and 14.98% currently, a 0.06% decrease, while the renewal segment moved from 21.85% to 21.95%, a 0.46% increase. This indicates the stronger movement was in renewals, while new business was essentially flat to slightly weaker.

Across the portfolio period from 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-01, fictional competitors all showed modest upward price-index movement while maintaining unchanged rank positions. Northgate Cover remained rank 1 with a price-index movement of 2.62%, Meridian Insure remained rank 2 with movement of 2.37%, and Bracken Mutual remained rank 3 with movement of 2.43%. This indicates stable relative market positioning alongside moderate market-wide price firming rather than rank disruption. 

Retrieved market intelligence was consistent with that pattern. A market report noted that these fictional competitors had each firmed personal motor renewal pricing by roughly 2% to 3% over the past quarter, with no fictional competitor reducing pricing in that window, and described the overall market position as consistent with a modest portfolio-wide pricing adjustment rather than an aggressive move. Repair-cost reporting also stated that parts and labour costs for common personal motor repairs had risen materially over the past twelve months, which was associated with wider claims-severity inflation across the industry. 

Broker evidence suggested the portfolio remained competitively positioned relative to fictional peers despite modest recent increases across the market. Brokers also reported that an earlier 2% portfolio-level renewal increase coincided with limited customer pushback and no material shift in quote volumes. Customer feedback was similarly calm: most renewal comments focused on claims-handling speed and overall satisfaction, while only a small minority referenced price and there was no concentrated pattern of fairness or affordability complaints in this period. 

Overall, fictional competitor movement and retrieved intelligence together point to a market environment where modest pricing increases coincided with stable competitive ordering, continued broker support, and limited observable customer price sensitivity in this period.

On 2024-06-01, the portfolio recorded one prior pricing action: a 2.0% renewal price increase at portfolio level. The recorded rationale was to offset early claims-inflation signals. This action was associated with a 0.6% decrease in conversion and a 1.0% decrease in loss ratio.

recommendation.rationale: A modest increase appears supportable because claims performance weakened while trading indicators and market context remained broadly stable. The loss ratio moved from 71.8% to 82.4%, indicating materially weaker profitability, and the claims specialist also reported higher average severity and incurred loss with broadly stable frequency, so deterioration was associated more with claim cost than volume [claims-north_west-2025-12-01]. At the same time, quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 22.0% and renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 88.1%, which suggests no clear evidence of current trading stress in aggregate [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01]. External positioning is also consistent with a modest upward move: tracked competitors showed average price-index movement of +2.5%, and supporting market, broker, repair-cost, and feedback evidence described moderate market firming, stable competitive positioning, repair-cost inflation, limited broker pushback, and no concentrated pattern of price complaints [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-market-2025-11, doc-repair-cost-2025-10, doc-broker-2025-12, doc-broker-2025-09, doc-feedback-2025-11]. The proposed 2% to 4% range stays within the stated policy limit and is directionally consistent with the prior recorded +2.0% pricing action [pricing-history-2024-06-01].
counter_evidence: Quote-to-sale conversion improved slightly from 21.9% to 22.0%, which means current aggregate conversion does not itself indicate a need for urgent corrective pricing action [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01].
Renewal retention was broadly stable at 88.0% to 88.1%, so customer stickiness has not weakened materially in the measured period [retention-north_west-2025-12-01].

The conversion specialist reported that average quoted premium was slightly lower while conversion improved slightly, and new business conversion was essentially flat to slightly weaker, so trading performance is mixed rather than uniformly strong [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01].

The prior +2.0% pricing action was associated with a 0.6% decrease in conversion, so another increase may coincide with some trading softening even though the same record also noted a 1.0% decrease in loss ratio [pricing-history-2024-06-01].

Market intelligence described the environment as consistent with a modest pricing adjustment rather than an aggressive move, which argues against using the full policy limit without further support [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-market-2025-11].

Customer feedback was calm rather than explicitly price-insensitive, so the absence of concentrated complaints should not be treated as proof that all segments would absorb an increase equally well [doc-feedback-2025-11].
conditions: Keep any proposed adjustment within a modest range aligned to observed competitor movement and the policy limit [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01].

A qualified analyst should review segment-level impacts, especially because the conversion specialist reported renewals were firmer while new business was essentially flat to slightly weaker [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01].
Monitor post-change conversion and retention closely given the recorded prior association between a +2.0% increase and a 0.6% decrease in conversion [pricing-history-2024-06-01].

Give particular attention to whether claims severity trends remain elevated, since the claims deterioration was associated with higher claim cost rather than higher frequency [claims-north_west-2025-12-01].
Requires explicit approval from a qualified pricing analyst before any action; the copilot cannot execute a pricing change.
